full_judgment: 6. Respondent, though a person in the service of the appellants' bank, did not, nor could he have, come to the Administrative Tribunal seeking redress against his termination for two reasons. He was terminated in 1981 when no persons in the service of any statutory authority, such as the Rupali Bank, were brought into the ambit of section 4 of the Act; such persons were brought in from 25 September 1984, as pointed out above. Secondly, no application of any person in the service of the Republic or of statutory body shall be entertained by the Administrative Tribunal, as provided in this section itself, unless it is made within six months from the date of the order or decision of the authority complained against. Sub-section (2) of section 4 of course provides that in case the order or decision complained of may be varied, reversed or modified by a "higher administrative authority" under any law in force, then the period of six months' limitation will be counted from the date of decision of the higher administrative authority. This is, however, not the respondent's case. Before filing his suit in 1987 he had spent about six years' time seeking remedies before persons and authorities not contemplated in sub-section (2). His case, therefore, goes out of the ambit of the Administrative Tribunal. His case will be governed by the law which was applicable to him and was in force at the time of his termination in 1981.
